## Incremental protocol change enforced unconditionally breaks released counterpart (P0)

Pattern: In a split client/provider rollout (enhanced-settings, Task 1), the client increment started requiring a new response field (`applied is True` receipt) on every save, ungated by the feature flag (`enhanced_settings`). The supported released provider (Git tag `eval-release`, `provider/settings.py`) returns only `{"ok": True}`, so every ordinary save raises even though the provider already persisted the values — client/server state diverge.

Masking signal: the unit test stub was edited from the released response shape to the new unreleased shape (`{"ok": True, "applied": True}`), hiding the regression.

Review check: when a diff adds a required protocol field/receipt, verify against the released counterpart snapshot (README names `eval-release` as baseline; provider source only in git history), confirm the requirement is gated behind the flag / tolerant of absence, and keep a test using the exact released response shape.
